questions.prompt: You c-bet KQ on K72 rainbow. The turn is a 2. Your hand…

choices.text: Is still top pair, but the deuce pairs the board and counterfeits some two pair less than a flush card would.
Is now the worst hand automatically

questions.explanation: Pairing the deuce is a small change. You still have a strong one pair. It is not a flush completing.

questions.prompt: You have the nut flush draw on the flop and the turn is a blank. Your draw…

choices.text: Still has about 9 outs, roughly 18% to come on the river.

questions.explanation: A blank does not fill the draw and does not add flush outs. One card left means outs times about 2.

questions.prompt: The turn pairs the top card. Who gains trips?

choices.text: Players who had that card in their hand, which is more often the preflop raiser on an ace-high board.
Only the small blind, by rule
Only pocket pairs that do not match the ace

questions.explanation: If the ace pairs, Ax in the raiser’s range makes trips. The caller has fewer aces.

questions.prompt: A turn four-straight (9 on QJT) means…

choices.text: Any eight or king already had the straight, and one-pair hands just got much worse.
The board cannot be a straight

questions.explanation: Queen-jack-ten-nine is four to a straight. Kings and eights made it. Do not keep betting ace-high.
